exposure: Body mass index (BMI) at beginning of pregnancy
cohort: The study included 2034 women from 2015 until 2018.
finding: Exceeding recommended gestational weight gain was associated with complications in pregnancy and labor, as well as higher neonatal birth weight.
mod_finding: Women with gestational weight gain exceeding recommendations were at higher risk of labor induction and unplanned cesarean section, and had a lower incidence of spontaneous vaginal birth.
